question: What shift structure should the schedule use for waiters?

options.text: Waiters work fixed-length shifts that start at the beginning of one of the listed time intervals.
Waiters can be assigned to any consecutive block of time intervals, with no fixed shift length.
Waiters work standard shifts such as 8 hours, but start times can be chosen freely.

rationale: The business facts say each waiter works a continuous 8-hour shift, and the demand table is organized into fixed time intervals. Option A best matches this by using fixed-length shifts starting at the beginning of one of those listed intervals, which is the natural scheduling structure for this problem.

question: How long is each waiter's fixed shift?

options.text: Each shift lasts 4 hours, covering exactly one of the listed time intervals.
Each shift lasts 8 hours, covering two consecutive listed time intervals.
Each shift lasts 12 hours, covering three consecutive listed time intervals.

rationale: The private business facts state that each waiter works a continuous 8-hour shift every day. Since the listed time intervals are 4 hours each, an 8-hour shift covers two consecutive listed intervals.

question: Can a waiter be assigned to more than one shift in the schedule?

options.text: Each waiter works exactly one shift.
A waiter can work multiple shifts, and the total number of waiters employed counts each person once.
A waiter can work multiple shifts, but each shift assignment counts as a separate employment.

rationale: The objective is to minimize the total number of waiters employed, and each waiter works a continuous 8-hour shift every day. This implies each employed waiter is assigned to exactly one shift, so option A fits the business meaning.

question: Which start times are allowed for the 8-hour shifts?

options.text: Shifts can start at the beginning of any of the six listed time intervals, including 22:00.
Shifts can start only at 6:00, 10:00, 14:00, and 18:00.
Shifts can start only at 2:00, 6:00, 10:00, and 14:00.

rationale: The demand table has six listed 4-hour intervals, and an 8-hour shift covers two consecutive intervals. Allowing shifts to start at the beginning of any listed interval, including 22:00, is consistent with the supplied facts and does not exclude any valid start time.

question: Are waiters interchangeable across all shifts, or do some have restrictions?

options.text: All waiters are interchangeable and can be assigned to any shift.
Some waiters have availability restrictions that limit which shifts they can work.
Some waiters have skill or role restrictions that limit which shifts they can work.

rationale: The supplied business facts describe only shift length, continuous 8-hour shifts, interval coverage requirements, and minimizing total waiters. No availability, skill, or role restrictions are mentioned, so treating all waiters as interchangeable is the closest match.
